title: 3D Printed Porous Cellulose Nanocomposite Hydrogel Scaffolds
protocol: Dilute a 17 wt% suspension of cellulose nanocrystals to 2 wt% by adding distilled water to make a total volume of 2 L.
Mix the diluted suspension thoroughly using ultrasonication and use smaller batches (250-300 mL) for efficient mixing.
Pass the sonified suspension through the homogenizer 10 times at a pressure of 500-600 bar.
Concentrate the 2 wt% cellulose nanocrystals gel to 11 wt% through centrifugations at 24,500 x g for 1.5 h.
Decant water out in between every 30 min.
Prepare a homogeneous solution of 6 wt% sodium alginate (SA) in distilled water at 60 °C under continuous stirring.
Prepare a homogeneous solution of 12 wt% gelatin (Gel) in distilled water at 60 °C under continuous stirring.
Store the matrix solutions in the refrigerator.
Prepare a solution of 3 wt% calcium chloride in distilled water at room temperature under continuous stirring.
Prepare a solution of 3 wt% glutaraldehyde in distilled water at room temperature under continuous stirring.
Prepare 40 mL of hydrogel ink by mixing 11 wt% CNC, 6 wt% SA and 12 wt% Gel in a polystyrene container.
Heat the mixture to 40 °C and mix with a spatula until a smooth paste is obtained.
Transfer the mixture into a 60 mL syringe.
Pass the mixture through a series of nozzles with diameters of 800 µm, followed by 600 µm and 400 µm into another 60 mL syringe using a mechanical clamp.
Gently centrifuge the syringe filled with hydrogel ink at 4,000 x g to remove trapped air.
Perform rheological properties measurement of hydrogel ink using a smooth cone-on-plate geometry CP25-2-SN7617, diameter 25 mm, 2° nominal angle and gap height 0.05 mm at 25 °C.
Turn on the rheometer, air compressor and temperature control box.
Initialize the software.
Mount the measuring tool in the rheometer and set zero-gap.
Extrude approximately 1 mL of hydrogel ink onto the rheometer platform.
Measure viscosity as a function of shear rate from 0.001 to 1,000.
Clean the rheometer platform and measuring tool.
Extrude 1 mL of fresh hydrogel ink on the rheometer platform.
Measure storage moduli (G′) and loss moduli (G″) as a function of shear stress at a frequency of 1 Hz.
Select the shear stress range from 103 to 107.
Copy the data into a text file.
Plot rheological curves in logarithmic scale.
Download an STL file of a solid cube from thingsinverse.com.
Open the downloaded STL file in Cura software.
Move the loaded model to X/Y/Z : 0/0/0 mm.
Click Scale, uncheck box for uniform scaling and set dimensions to X/Y/Z : 20/20/20 mm.
Rotate the cube by 45° in the XY plane.
In the side panel, select nozzle size of 0.4 mm and paste the profile.
Select Discov3ry complete as the printer.
Insert the transfer tube into the nozzle holder and connect 400 μm nozzle to it.
Level the build plate to get the correct distance between the build plate and nozzle.
Load the centrifuged syringe into the cartridge and connect it to the other side of the transfer tube.
Insert the SD card into the printer.
Select Purge fast and start purging the hydrogel ink until it starts to extrude from the nozzle.
Continue purging for 2-3 min to obtain a homogeneous flow.
From the SD card, select the saved files for uniform and gradient porosity scaffolds.
Start printing the selected files.
Keep an eye on the extrusion rate during printing.
If needed, adjust the speed and flow rate accordingly.
For smaller pore size, use faster speed combined with low flow rate (50 mm/s and 70%).
After 3D printing is complete, gently add drops of 3 wt% CaCl2 to the scaffold until it becomes completely wet.
Wait for 5 min before transferring the scaffold.
Very carefully transfer the scaffold from the printer to a 50 mL container filled with 3 wt% CaCl2.
Leave the scaffold in the CaCl2 solution overnight.
Wash thoroughly with distilled water after removing from CaCl2 solution.
Transfer the scaffold to a 50 mL container filled with 3 wt% glutaraldehyde.
Leave the scaffold in glutaraldehyde overnight.
Wash thoroughly and store the 3D printed scaffold in distilled water.
Fill the container equipped with submersible compression base plate with 2 L of water.
Start the heating system to reach 37 °C for compression testing.
Initialize Bluehill Universal software and set up the testing method.
Select rectangular specimen geometry and choose the option to enter dimensions before each test.
Set the strain rate to 2 mm/min and end of result at 80% compressive strain with a force limit of 90 N.
In the Measurement section, select force, displacement, compressive stress, and compressive strain.
Choose the option to export data as text files for future plotting.
Set the zero extension point by using jog controls to lower the crosshead plate close to the base plate.
Measure and note the dimensions of the samples to be tested.
When the water temperature reaches 37 °C, place the sample on the base plate.
Secure the sample by moving the crosshead plate so that it starts to touch the sample.
Move the water bath up so that the plates with the sample in-between them are immersed in water.
Enter the sample name and dimensions.
Start the test.
After completion of the test, first move the water bath down then raise the crosshead plate.
Remove the sample and its pieces if any.
Clean both the plates and load a new sample.
Repeat the process for all samples to be tested.
Export raw data after completing tests on all samples.
Plot compressive stress vs. compressive strain curves.
Determine the compressive tangent modulus at strain values of 1-5% and 25-30%.
